 Learn more Oscar Health plans to expand its individual health insurance coverage offerings into one new state and 140 new counties next year even as rivals exit the market. Oscar, which is one of the largest providers of individual health insurance coverage under the Affordable Care Act also known as Obamacare, said it is expanding into South Carolina for 2027, giving the company a 21-state footprint. Oscar Health plans to expand its individual health insurance coverage offerings into one new state and 140 new counties next year even as rivals exit the market. 
 Oscar, which is one of the largest providers of individual health insurance coverage under the Affordable Care Act also known as Obamacare, said it is expanding into South Carolina for 2027, giving the company a 21-state footprint. 
 The moves by Oscar comes as larger rivals have pulled out of the Obamcare market. Cigna earlier this year disclosed plans to exit the individual health insurance business, leaving about 369,00 health plan members in 11 states looking for new coverage in 2027. And a year ago, CVS Health announced plans to exit the individual health insurance business, leaving about 1 million Aetna members in 17 states looking for new coverage for this year. 
 Those big name departures have left an opening for Oscar. Open enrollment for Obamacare begins November 1 and runs through December 15 for coverage that begins January 1, 2027. 
 "The individual market is built for everyone from entrepreneurs launching businesses to people working part-time to employees and gig workers of companies large and small," Oscar Health chief executive officer Mark Bertolini said in announcing the expansion Tuesday. 
 Oscar has been getting its costs under control and improving its bottom line in the last year or so. The company reported more than $1 billion in net income for the first half of this year. 
 The company is also rolling out several new products like a new plan called "RetireEase," which the company said "simplifies the transition from early retirement to Medicare." And the company is expanding its product with the large Midwest grocery and pharmacy chain Hy-Vee beyond the Des Moines market to other parts of Iowa as well as Nebraska, Missouri and Kansas. 
 "Hy-Vee Health with Oscar" is part of a wave of health benefit offerings known as individual coverage health reimbursement arrangements , or ICHRAs. Such plans involve employers paying their workers a set amount each month to purchase health insurance on their own via a carrier, broker or government exchange. The company said Hy-Vee Health with Oscar is also available to individual purchasers of healthcare on the government exchange in those states. 
 Founded in 2012, Oscar had struggled to turn consistent quarterly profits, but Mark Bertolini -- the former chief executive officer of Aetna who was tapped as Oscar's top executive in March of 2023 -- and his team – have delivered on their promises as they remain bullish on the individual health insurance. 
 Story Continues "We listen to what they want, what makes their day-to-day easier, and deliver healthcare with intuitive technology that fits their lifestyle," Bertolini said. "Every Oscar product helps people take control of their health at every stage of life. It's healthcare made-for-me."
